fields.claim_quote: Given that a graph may generally admit multiple transitive reductions, prove that G possesses a unique transitive reduction if and only if G is acyclic.
fields.complete_source:
Solution:
Let G be a directed graph. Define the transitive closure GT as the directed
graph sharing the same vertex set as G, where an edge u →v exists in GT if and only if
there is a directed path from u to v in G. Furthermore, define a transitive reduction of G to
be a graph with the minimum number of edges such that its transitive closure is identical to
GT. Given that a graph may generally admit multiple transitive reductions, prove that G
possesses a unique transitive reduction if and only if G is acyclic.
Solution.
We work with finite directed graphs (digraphs), with no parallel edges; a directed path
is a sequence of vertices of positive length with all edges oriented consistently along the
sequence.
For a digraph G = (V, E), its transitive closure GT is the digraph on V with edge set
ET = {(u, v) ∈V × V : there is a directed path u ⇝v in G}.
A transitive reduction of G is a digraph H = (V, F) with the minimum possible number of
edges such that HT = GT.
We begin with the classical part of the statement, valid for acyclic graphs.
Theorem 1 (DAG case). If G is acyclic, then G has a unique transitive reduction.
Proof. When G is a directed acyclic graph (DAG), the reachability relation
u ⪯v
⇐⇒
there is a directed path u ⇝v
is a partial order on V . Its cover relation,
u ≺· v
⇐⇒
u ≺v and there is no w with u ≺w ≺v,
defines the Hasse diagram H = (V, {(u, v) : u ≺· v}).
It is a standard fact that the
transitive closure of the Hasse diagram recovers the partial order: HT = GT (see e.g. any
text on posets).
We claim H is the unique transitive reduction. First, minimality: if an edge (u, v) of H
were deleted, there would be no path from u to v in the remaining graph, because any such
path would yield an intermediate w with u ≺w ≺v, contradicting

fields.witness:
2-cycle a⇄b: unique reduction, cyclic

Take V={a,b} and E={(a,b),(b,a)}. This graph is cyclic. Its transitive closure requires reachability a↝b and b↝a (and self-reachability if the convention includes it). Any equivalent digraph on these two vertices must contain edge a→b and edge b→a; loops cannot create cross reachability. These two edges suffice, so the unique minimum equivalent digraph is the same 2-cycle. Thus uniqueness does not imply acyclicity.
